sections.title: SURVEY BASIS
sections.body:
**Archive interval:** Four production cycles reviewed against control-house environmental and utility logs

**Instrumentation:** Fixed active near-infrared reflectance cameras, portable active reflectance meter, leaf-temperature references, independent illuminance loggers, and isolated power-quality monitors

**Study boundary:** Three enclosed growth bays and one matched control bay within an otherwise ordinary horticultural complex.

sections.title: OBSERVED VARIANCE
sections.body:
**Canopy response:** The three study bays entered a synchronized high-assimilation spectral state during seven unprogrammed overnight intervals. The control bay did not. Measured photosynthetically active radiation remained below detector threshold.

**Physiological confirmation:** Portable fluorometry and gas-exchange sampling confirmed five events. Carbon-dioxide uptake increased and leaf temperature fell by 1.1 to 1.6 degrees Celsius while the bays remained dark.

**Systems comparison:** Lighting, irrigation, ventilation, carbon-dioxide, control-network, and utility logs showed no common command, interruption, or unmetered input at the onset times.

**Mass balance:** Destructive samples taken after two events carried 1.8 and 2.2 percent more dry mass than matched controls. The excess was absent 36 hours later without recorded shedding or measurable change in collected drain water.

sections.title: INTERPRETIVE LIMITS
sections.body:
**Ordinary explanations tested:** Shared sensor calibration, undocumented control-network traffic, thermal lag, cultivar response, stray illumination, and sampling bias were addressed through independent instruments, isolated controls, and blinded dry-mass handling.

**Confirmed exception:** The monitored canopies entered a photosynthetically active state without measurable incident light and produced a temporary dry-mass increase without a recorded carbon, water, or nutrient source. No transfer pathway was identified.

sections.title: DISPOSITION
sections.body:
**Finding:** Repeatable light-independent assimilation response with a reversible positive dry-mass residual across three isolated bays

**Action:** Maintain continuous isolated logging. The next confirmed interval requires sealed-atmosphere sampling, duplicate photon counters, and pre-weighed tissue custody. Affected material is excluded from ordinary production disposition pending control-office review.

**Review status:** Active on event trigger. Automatic instrument capture remains in service.

**Release limit:** Product, operator, and property identifiers are outside this archive copy.
